findings.finding: `except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):` misses `OverflowError`, which the existing validators can raise via `math.isfinite` for sufficiently large JSON integers. Such a malformed artifact escapes `freshness_report`, causing the endpoint to replace the entire report with `unavailable` instead of marking only the offending component `stale` as required by the API contract.
Provider exception logging can disclose the EODHD API key through credential-bearing request URLs.
The Requests timeout bounds individual socket waits, not total probe duration; a trickling provider can hold the freshness cache lock and a worker thread indefinitely

The provider probe still has no end-to-end deadline. Evidence: `expected_session, _ = await asyncio.to_thread(`. Removing `asyncio.wait_for` means a non-returning provider call blocks the report and freshness-cache lock indefinitely. The new Requests timeout covers connection and intervals between socket reads—not DNS resolution or total elapsed time—so a slow-dripping response can still hang the probe permanently. The prior bounded-probe finding therefore remains open.
